items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Well, no. Both of them, Don -- in fact, I later on played with Don in another band, but I couldn't see leaving California.

ctx.x: We were talking about the shows -- some of the stage shows that used to come to the club.

Yes. One of the stage shows I remember was a show that came out with Don Redman. And he was fronting McKinney's Cotton Pickers Band at that time. And on the floor -- the show was Broomfield and Greely, was a dance team from the East. And their show was on.

It was during this time that things began to happen with me. It was during this show that one of my peculiar attitudes, I will say, came about. One of the members of this band was a very, very famous person. And we all idolized him as a musician. And heretofore I had never had much experience with the antics of musicians, and so I hadn't paid too much attention.

items.title: 52986_Lawrence Brown oral history interview
items.q: Don Redman Redmond was the leader of the band and we played different theaters

ctx.x: Now, let me see. That was before CBS. We did a -- travelled the Eastern circuit there for awhile, I must've been there for about six months in the bad. Don Redman Redmond was the leader of the band and we played different theaters, Earle Theater in Washington and different theaters around that area.
